result:
Good — all 3 tests pass (the pre-existing search test plus my two new `posts.update` assertions), and typecheck is clean.

I fixed the bug in `app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts`: `update()` was building a raw `302` `Response` by hand instead of using `this.redirect()`. Per the Fetch spec, a `302` redirect only downgrades `POST` to `GET`; a `PUT` request stays `PUT` after following it, so the browser kept re-`PUT`ing `/posts/:id` forever — the `ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS` loop from the report (the save itself succeeded before the loop started, which is why reloading showed the new content). Swapping in `this.redirect(`/posts/${post.id}`)` matches `store()`/`destroy()` and correctly issues a `303`, which Inertia's client follows as a fresh `GET` navigation. I added a regression test in `tests/PostController.test.ts` (`posts.update` describe block) asserting the update response is `303` with `Location: /posts/:id`, and confirmed `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` both pass.
